# Kagami

> Kagami is an open-source, deception-based defence against AI-driven attacks on web applications. It places
> tripwires that only attackers touch (planted credentials, decoy routes, decoy fields, sealed IDs), records the
> attack, and can contain the attacking machine so it never reaches the application again. The engine is Rust
> compiled to WebAssembly and shared by every language. Node and Express are supported today. It needs one
> self-generated secret, KAGAMI_SECRET, and no account.

Coding agents that are adding Kagami to an application should follow the integration guide step by step and finish
with `npx @agenticslabs/kagami doctor --json`.

## Integrate

- [Integration guide for AI coding agents](docs/ai/integrate.md): exact steps, checks and what to tell the owner
- [Getting started](docs/guides/getting-started.md): the same steps for people
- [Behind a proxy or CDN](docs/guides/behind-a-proxy.md): setting the client address correctly
- [Troubleshooting](docs/guides/troubleshooting.md): every doctor result and its fix

## Concepts

- [How Kagami works](docs/guides/how-it-works.md): request lifecycle, tripwires, deception, containment

- [Cloudflare](docs/guides/cloudflare.md): blocking contained machines at Cloudflare's edge, built in
